story.head: Holmström lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Ben Hutton struck first for the Islanders just under two minutes in. There were six goals in the second period alone. Bo Horvat made it 2-0 on the power play early in the period, in his 900th NHL game. Nikita Nesterenko got the Ducks on the board just over a minute later. The Isles’ Logan Stanley left early in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a lower-body injury. Simon Holmström stretched the lead to 3-1 early in the period. Holmström and Mitchell Chaffee scored two minutes apart midway through the period to make it 5-1. Cutter Gauthier cut the Islanders’ lead to 5-2 late in the period, his eighth straight game with a goal. Holmström completed his hat trick early in the third to make it 6-2 for the Islanders. Mathew Barzal played his first game of the season, after missing the first 18, and picked up an assist. Matthew Schaefer finished with three assists.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Semyon Varlamov made 26 saves for the Islanders, and Lukáš Dostál allowed six goals on 25 shots. The Islanders moved to 9-6-4 and climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Ducks fell to 10-9-1, third in the Pacific.
